\[
\lambda_s = \lambda_0 f^{s},\quad \theta_k = \frac{180 k}{n},\quad \sigma_s = \frac{\lambda_s}{\pi}\sqrt{\frac{\ln 2}{2}}\,\frac{2^b + 1}{2^b - 1},\quad M(p) = \max_{s,k} \left| (g_{s,k} \star I)(p) \right|
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\lambda_0\): The smallest wavelength
- \(f\): The scale factor
- \(n\): The number of orientations
- \(b\): The bandwidth in octaves
- \(g_{s,k}\): The Gabor kernel of scale s and orientation k

Scale s has the wavelength lambda_0 f^s, and orientation k the angle 180 k / n. Sigma follows from the bandwidth b in octaves, as in scikit-image. Each g_{s,k} is a Gabor kernel, and M is the largest magnitude. The mean output averages the magnitudes instead. The angle output gives theta_k of the strongest filter. When several filters are within a relative 1e-9 of the largest magnitude, the first in the order of the bank wins. This makes exact ties, such as theta and 180 - theta next to a mirrored border, independent of rounding.
